title: Bina and tevuna: abstract understanding, and the power to apply it
overview:
Chapter 1 taught *hisbonenus* as it rises to *chachma*; chapter 2 brings it down to the emotions and to action. *Bina* has two levels. *Bina* itself is abstract understanding: the *tafsan* with a sharp grasp, the *Gemara* learned *b'iyun* that yields no *halacha*, pure science, an idea that is still a *hiyuli*. *Tevuna*, the light of *bina* spreading out, is applied understanding, and it comes from *kelita*: absorbing the idea until it is the way you think. Then, like the shepherd who draws deep water up to the sheep, the man of *tevuna* can rule in a particular case, explain the depth simply, and feel it in his heart.

*Tevuna* has its own depth, length and width; its letters spell *ben u'vas*, because the emotions are born from *tevuna*, the lower mother, which also gives them their intellect and keeps them going. The way to get it is the double *nun* of *hisbonenus*: go over the idea again and again, in your own words, until it sinks in.

terms.gloss: applied understanding: the light of bina spreading out into application, into the emotions, and into explaining it to others
absorption: the idea sinks in until it becomes the way you think, the root of tevuna
a man of tevuna, who draws the deep waters up so that anyone can drink
a grasper: a quick, sharp mind whose understanding stays in the theory
raw potential: an idea of which nobody yet knows what will come out
grasping a concept while it stays outside of you, as opposed to kelita
son and daughter, the letters of tevuna: love and fear, born from tevuna
the lower mother: tevuna, the womb that actually gives birth to the middos
the upper mother: bina, the real source of the middos but not their direct source
"and so": the conclusion that applies the idea to me, which turns understanding into emotion
thought itself, the letters of thought, coming from Malchus of tevuna
the straight, long nun: the length; the second nun of hisbonenus, which carries bina into tevuna

sections.title: Tevuna is bina spreading out: the man of tevuna draws up the deep waters
sections.summary: *Bina* has two levels, *bina* and *tevuna*. *Bina* is abstract understanding; *tevuna* is applied understanding, the light of *bina* spreading out, and it comes when the idea is absorbed so well that it becomes yours. Then, like the shepherd who draws deep water up to the sheep, a man of *tevuna* can bring the depth out so simply that it is as if it was never deep.

phrases.he: (ב) והנה ידוע שיש בבינה עצמה ב' מדרגות, בינה ותבונה,
phrases.en: It's known that *bina* itself has two levels: *bina* and *tevuna*.

phrases.he: וענין התבונה הוא בחינת התפשטות אור הבינה
phrases.en: The idea of *tevuna* is the spreading out of the light of *bina*.
Like it says in the *Zohar*,

phrases.he: דאבא ואמא תתאין הם ישראל סבא ותבונה,
phrases.en: the lower father and mother, meaning the lower *chachma* and *bina*, are called *Yisroel Saba*, grandfather Israel, and *tevuna*.

blocks.text: In the first chapter we explained *hisbonenus* (contemplation): that it is *iyun* (close analysis), how it relates to *omek hadaas* (the depth of *daas*), and what a *ma'amik* (one who delves) is. That was the *Chabad* (*chachma*, *bina* and *daas*) of *Chabad*. Now we explain how *hisbonenus* brings you not only up to *chachma* and *Keser* (crown), but down to the *middos* (emotional attributes) of the *sechel* (intellect), and from there to actual emotions and actual *maaseh* (action).

**It's known that bina itself has two levels: bina and tevuna.** *Tanya* mentions *tevuna*, but most people do not know what it is unless they learn a *maamar* (discourse) on the difference. *Bina* (understanding), explained in the last chapter, is making distinctions, seeing each part of a thing and all its details. *Tevuna* is the power of applied understanding, as opposed to abstract understanding.

**The idea of tevuna is the spreading out of the light of bina.** The *Zohar* says that **the lower father and mother, meaning the lower chachma and bina, are called Yisroel Saba, grandfather Israel, and tevuna**: the *hispashtus* (spreading forth) of *chachma* and of *bina*, the way they go out of them. Now, what causes this spreading out?

phrases.he: מצד קליטתה היטב בכלי המקבל ההשגה דבינה,
phrases.en: This is because the idea is very well received, or very well absorbed, into the vessel that receives the understanding of *bina*.

phrases.he: על כן מתפשט בה להביאה בכמה ענינים נבדלים מעצם ההשגה,
phrases.en: Therefore, the idea spreads out in it to come into many, many different things that are separate from the abstract understanding.
And this is what is called a man of *tevuna*.

phrases.he: כמו מים עמוקים כו' איש תבונה ידלנה.
phrases.en: Like it says in the verse, deep waters... a man of *tevuna* can draw it out.

blocks.text: The light of *bina* spreads out **because the idea is very well received, or very well absorbed, into the vessel that receives the understanding of bina. Therefore, the idea spreads out in it to come into many, many different things that are separate from the abstract understanding.** When the idea really sinks in and becomes one with you, it is yours, and you can apply it outside the textbooks in all different ways. **This is what is called a man of tevuna**: deep waters, **a man of tevuna can draw it out.**

phrases.en: the deep waters,
that is the depth of *bina*,
The depth of *bina* remains hidden in yourself.
and a man of *tevuna*,
only such a person that has this type of understanding
can draw it out,
and can draw it from its hiddenness,
to bring it out into application
many different ways,
to quench the thirst of the *mekablim*.

phrases.he: כמו הדולה מים עמוקים להשקות הצאן כו'
phrases.en: like somebody that draws deep waters to water sheep.
and this is like what we see,
tangibly,

phrases.he: שבהיות השכל והסברא עמוקים ביותר מהכיל בהשגת אדם,
phrases.en: that when an idea or a *sevara* is very deep, and it's too deep for a person to grasp,

phrases.he: הנקרא מים עמוקים כו', שהוא בחינת עומק המושג הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that's the depth of understanding that we discussed in the last *perek*,
which the length and the width of the idea come out from that point.

blocks.text: **The deep waters, that is the depth of bina**, **remains hidden in yourself**, like the *omek hamusag* (the depth of the concept), which cannot be explained directly, only through the length and the width. **Only such a person that has this type of understanding can draw it out**, **from its hiddenness, to bring it out into application** in **many different ways**, **to quench the thirst of the mekablim** (the receivers).

blocks.title: The shepherd at the deep well
blocks.text: The sheep are thirsty, and the shepherd gets them water from a very deep well. He lowers a bucket and brings it up: the exact same water, but now not deep at all. *Yidlena* means to draw it, like with a bucket; *yishavena* means to pour it out into a trough.

**And this is like what we see, tangibly**: when an idea or a *sevara* is **too deep for a person to grasp**, it is called deep waters, **the depth of understanding that we discussed in the last perek**, which **the length and the width of the idea come out from**.

phrases.en: And specifically a person that has this power of *tevuna* can draw out this depth.

phrases.he: פירוש שיוציא לאור בחינת העלם העומק המושג
phrases.en: He's able to bring out to light, in order to reveal, this hidden depth of the idea,
until a person's mind can grasp it, can understand it,
as if it wasn't deep at all.

phrases.he: כמו הדולה מים עמוקים שמקרב את העומק כו'
phrases.en: Like the shepherd that draws the water from the well, that now brings it close to the sheep, as if it wasn't deep at all.
And based on this,
we must say

phrases.he: שכח התבונה הוא כח המתפשט מכח הבינה להביא עומקה לגילוי למטה למקבלים כו'
phrases.en: that the power of *tevuna* is the ability to bring out the understanding of *bina*, to bring its depth so that it should be understood to other people, to the *mekabel*.

blocks.text: **A person that has this power of tevuna can draw out this depth. He's able to bring out to light** this **hidden depth of the idea, until a person's mind can grasp it**, **as if it wasn't deep at all.** It becomes a simple idea, **like the shepherd that draws the water from the well** and **brings it close to the sheep**: now it is right in front of them.

**And based on this, we must say that the power of tevuna is the ability to bring out the understanding of bina, to bring its depth so that it should be understood to other people.** The power to teach an idea to someone who does not grasp it on his own, making it simpler for him, comes from *tevuna*.

sections.title: The tafsan: a sharp grasp that stays in the theory
sections.summary: Someone who is not a man of *tevuna* can still have a quick, sharp grasp, a *tafsan*, and yet his understanding stays in his own *bina*: he cannot teach it or apply it. Even its length and width are only the textbook's examples, all within the theory, and its depth stays hidden even to him.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כשאינו איש תבונות,
phrases.en: On the other hand, when somebody is not a man of *tevunos*,

phrases.he: גם שהוא בעל השגה במוח דבינה
phrases.en: even if he does understand personally, he's able to understand the idea with his faculty of *bina*,
which the world calls a *tafsan*,

phrases.he: יוכל להיות שהשגתו נשארת רק כמו שהיא בעצם, במוח הבינה שלו
phrases.en: it can be that his understanding will remain the way it is, just in his faculty of *bina*,
that's called just his spirit of understanding,

phrases.he: ולא יבוא ממנה שום התפשטות למטה
phrases.en: and no application will come out from it,

phrases.he: בענין נבדל שחוץ מן עצם ההשגה כלל
phrases.en: in any matter that's separate from the abstract understanding at all.

blocks.text: **On the other hand, when somebody is not a man of tevunos**, he does not absorb the idea so that he can bring it out simply. **Even if he does understand personally**, with **his faculty of bina, which the world calls a tafsan** (a grasper), with a quick, sharp mind, that does not mean he is able to teach it.

**It can be that his understanding will remain the way it is, just in his faculty of bina**: he cannot explain it to anyone or apply it; it stays abstract theory, **just his spirit of understanding**, **and no application will come out from it, in any matter that's separate from the abstract understanding at all.**

phrases.he: וגם שיש בהשגה אורך ורוחב ועומק כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: and even though the understanding of the theory itself has a length and a width and a depth,
even all of this, even the length and the width, are just part of the abstract understanding,
as it is, in its natural state.

phrases.he: אבל לא שיתגלה למטה בענין נבדל,
phrases.en: But it doesn't mean that it will be expressed in something separate,

phrases.he: ומכל שכן עומק המושג הרי נשאר בעומקו בהעלם לעצמו,
phrases.en: and for sure the depth of his understanding remains hidden to himself,
and even the length and the width
are all within the idea itself,
the way it is in its place alone.

blocks.text: **And even though the understanding of the theory itself has a length and a width and a depth**, even the length and the width **are just part of the abstract understanding, as it is**. That is the textbook: to explain the idea he needs *meshalim* (analogies) and examples, so the idea has all these parts, but it is all in the theory.

**But it doesn't mean that it will be expressed in something separate.** **And for sure the depth of his understanding remains hidden to himself**: he cannot explain it. **And even the length and the width are all within the idea itself**: it is all just theory.

sections.title: The example: a Talmudic pilpul that yields no ruling, an idea that is only hiyuli
sections.summary: Someone can learn a *Gemara* in depth, with all the *sevaros* of the commentators, and still not know the *halacha*: the reasoning stays an abstract thing that rules neither liable nor exempt. Such an idea is a *hiyuli*, of which nobody yet knows what will come out.

phrases.en: And an example for all of this:

phrases.he: הנה אנו רואים בעומק הפלפול בתלמוד וטעמים בסברות רבות כך וכך
phrases.en: when a person's learning *Gemara*, and they learn a whole *pilpul* with many different reasons and *sevaros*, one this way and one that way,
even when they understand it very well,

phrases.he: אבל לא יוכלו עדיין להוציא לאור מעצם השכל איזה פסק דין חייב או זכאי כלל

blocks.text: **And an example for all of this: when a person's learning Gemara, and they learn a whole pilpul with many different reasons and sevaros, one this way and one that way**, with all the *Rishonim* and *Acharonim* (the earlier and later commentators), **even when they understand it very well**, they still cannot bring out of the intellect itself any ruling, liable or exempt, at all.

A person can learn *Gemara* (the Talmud) *b'iyun* (in depth), understand it very well with all the *sevaros* (lines of reasoning), and, as is usually the case, not know the *halacha* (the law in practice) from it at all. They are almost opposite ways of learning: *Gemara b'iyun* goes into the depth, up, away from the practical; *halacha* goes down. Unless you specially learn the *Gemara l'halacha* (for the practical law), you will not see it: you have to "switch the whole direction of your thinking".

That is why, for a lot of people, when they start learning *semicha* (rabbinic ordination), it is a big change in their whole way of learning. They are used to learning *Gemara b'iyun* without learning it *l'halacha*, and all of a sudden now they are learning it *l'halacha*.

phrases.en: This means

phrases.he: שלא יוכל להוציא מתוך הסברה איזה חיוב על פי זה השכל ולא איזה זכות על פי זה השכל

blocks.text: **This means** that he cannot bring out of the reasoning any liability or any merit. He learns the *Gemara* and knows the *sevara* according to *Rashi*, according to *Tosfos*, the *Rosh*, the *Ran*, the *Rif*, the *Rambam*, the *Ramban*. But ask him, "Okay, so according to this *sevara*, how would it come out in this case?" and he does not know yet. Seeing how a *sevara* comes out practically is a whole other level of understanding.

phrases.he: כי עדיין אין השכל והסברה רק השכלה שכליות לבד,
phrases.en: Because right now, it's just an abstract, intellectual thing.

phrases.he: בלתי ימצא ממנו שום התפשטות בהטיות לענין נבדל הימנה,
שהוא לחייב על ידה או לזכות על ידה
phrases.en: which means to find guilt because of it or merit because of it.

blocks.text: **Because right now, it's just an abstract, intellectual thing**, with no spreading out or inclining toward anything separate: a *pilpul* about the definition of the liability. Is it a *gavra* (on the person), a *cheftza* (on the object), because of this, because of that?

blocks.title: The first inquiry in Bava Kama
blocks.text: Rabbi Walters remembers learning *Bava Kama*: a whole *chakira* (inquiry) whether you are liable for damage by your property because of the *he'eder hashmira* (the failure to guard it) or because of an actual obligation, a relationship to your money. Either way, you see no *nafka mina* (practical difference). Then you ask what the difference is, and they tell you: if somebody betroths a woman on condition that this is the reason for the law. "You know, that's what they tell you."

Right now they are after the thing itself and do not care what the practical thing is: "Afterwards, we'll see." So it will not come out to anything separate, **which means to find guilt because of it or merit because of it.**

phrases.en: This is like something that is a *hiyuli*, like an essence,

phrases.he: שלא נודע עדיין מה ימצא ממנה ומה יעשה בה
phrases.en: that we do not yet know what will come out from it or what can be done with it.
In Yiddish we would say: the idea itself as it is, meaning the abstract theory,

phrases.he: ער קאן מיט אים נישט טאן קיין זאך ניט
phrases.en: he can't do anything with it,

phrases.he: צו קערין לזכות או לחוב כו')
phrases.en: to lean the judgment to merit or to liability.

blocks.text:
**This is like something that is a hiyuli, like an essence**, like we explained in chapters 10 and 11 (*hiyuli*: raw potential), **that we do not yet know what will come out from it or what can be done with it.** We have no idea yet, because it could come out in so many different ways.

In Yiddish we would say: **the idea itself as it is, meaning the abstract theory**, just an abstract theory: **he can't do anything with it, to lean the judgment to merit or to liability.**

sections.title: The power of tevuna: application to a ruling, to the heart and to thought
sections.summary: *Tevuna* brings the abstract understanding down into what is separate from it: a ruling of guilty or innocent, an emotion in the heart, many ways of thinking it. *Bina* is pure science and *Gemara b'iyun*; *tevuna* is applied science, *halacha*, and knowing how to set up a kosher kitchen.

phrases.en: However,
the power of *tevuna* that spreads out from the faculty of *bina*:

phrases.he: היינו מה שביכולתו להביא עצם ההשגה לבחינת התפשטות למטה ממנה
phrases.en: it's in the ability of this power to bring the abstract understanding to application in something lower than it,
in anything separate from it,
whether that means to find the judgment of guilt or innocence,
or to bring it to an excitement in your heart, that you should have an emotional reaction because of this understanding,

phrases.he: וכן להביאה במחשבה בכמה אופנים שונים כו'.
phrases.en: and also to be able to bring it into thought in many different ways, that you should be able to explain the idea to yourself in all different ways, conceptualize it, even the depth of it, in many ways.

blocks.text: **However**, being stuck in abstract theory is only in *bina* itself. **The power of tevuna that spreads out from the faculty of bina** is **the ability of this power to bring the abstract understanding to application in something lower than it, in anything separate from it**: **to find the judgment of guilt or innocence**, **or to bring it to an excitement in your heart**, **and also to be able to bring it into thought in many different ways**, explaining the idea to yourself, even its depth, in all different ways.

So this is the general difference between *bina* and *tevuna*: *bina* is the abstract understanding, and it is still like a *hiyuli* to its applications; *tevuna* is the power of applied understanding.

It is the difference between somebody who learns *Gemara* just *l'iyun*, like a *pilpul*, and somebody who learns *halacha*. "And actually I think that it used to be that Chabad would stress learning *Gemara l'halacha*." Rabbi Walters is not sure whether there was a reason it changed, or it just became popular in the world to learn in the *pilpul* style. "But I don't know, I heard that that's the way that it was always done." It might say so in *Kuntres Etz HaChaim*.

blocks.title: Pure and applied science
blocks.text: It is like pure and applied science. Pure mathematics is just the theory, the numbers and the formulas, not applied to anything yet. Applied mathematics is engineering: figuring out the trajectories to send something to the moon, or, for a bridge, all the variables, the pressure, the wind, how an earthquake would affect the structure. That is the practical side of it.

blocks.title: Learning shechita in the Gemara and in the Shulchan Aruch
blocks.text: Learning *Shulchan Aruch* (the Code of Jewish Law) is a practical understanding: not the same as doing it, but an idea that relates to doing it. Learning the *Gemara* about *shechita* (ritual slaughter), you ask why this *shechita* is kosher and that one is not, looking for the real determinant, the key factor everything is based on. That search for the depth is *bina*; learning what to do practically is *tevuna*.

blocks.title: The hard steel knife
blocks.text: A lot of the things of *tevuna* are circumstantial. The main thing in *shechita* is that it cuts by the sharpness of the knife, not by ripping, not by your pressure. So practically you want a very sharp knife, of very hard steel so it will not nick, because a nick rips. But really you may *shecht* with anything sharp, and not even that sharp: you could go back and forth all day and it would be kosher, as long as you are not applying pressure and it is not ripping. The hard steel knife is a practical thing.

blocks.title: Setting up a kosher kitchen
blocks.text: You see this difference, between the abstract idea and a practical way to do it, between the way *bochurim* (yeshiva boys) and girls learn, say, *kashrus* (the kosher laws). Even *bochurim* learning *semicha* learn much more the theory. But setting up a kitchen so that it practically stays kosher, with separate dishes and separate burners, in a way that reduces the number of problems, "is a whole nother *chachma*": a whole other power of understanding.

sections.title: The middos within bina stay in theory; the man of tevuna brings the ruling out
sections.summary: *Bina* has emotions of its own, the intellect that leans to merit or to guilt, so it seems that *tevuna* is not needed. But those emotions stay hidden in the theory; only the man of *tevuna*, who has not just grasped the idea (*tefisa*) but absorbed it (*kelita*), can rule in a particular case and explain the depth to anyone.

phrases.en: However, seemingly we see
that seemingly *bina* itself has *middos*,
which are called the seven lower *sefiros* of *bina*.
And these are called the emotions of the intellect,

phrases.he: המטה כלפי זכות או שכל מטה כלפי חוב
phrases.en: an intellect that leans towards merit or an intellect that leans towards guilt.

blocks.text: **However, seemingly we see that seemingly bina itself has middos, which are called the seven lower sefiros of bina.** So why do we need *tevuna* as the application of *bina*? **And these are called the emotions of the intellect, an intellect that leans towards merit or an intellect that leans towards guilt**: the intellect tells you it is *chayav* (liable) or *patur* (exempt).

phrases.he: היינו כמו שהמדות שבשכל הן בעצם ההשגה עדיין בהעלם
phrases.en: So the emotions of *bina* itself are the emotions of the intellect the way they are in the abstract theory, and they're still hidden.

phrases.he: אבל להביא בחינת התגלותן בדבר נבדל,
phrases.en: But to be able to reveal them in something separate,

phrases.he: כמו להורות בענין מקרה דבר מה על פי השכל והסברא הזאת,
phrases.en: to say the ruling in a particular case based on this intellect and this logic,

phrases.he: להטות את המשפט של זה הענין לחסד וגבורה שבו דוקא,
phrases.en: to influence the judgment of this case to either the *chesed* or *gevura*,

phrases.he: הרי איש תבונה דווקא יוציא לאור מן המדות שבבינה כו'
phrases.en: specifically a person of *tevuna* is able to bring out the ruling from the emotions of *bina*.

blocks.text: **So the emotions of bina itself are the emotions of the intellect the way they are in the abstract theory, and they're still hidden.** **But to be able to reveal them in something separate, to say the ruling in a particular case based on this intellect and this logic, to influence the judgment of this case to either the chesed or gevura** (kindness or severity): **specifically a person of tevuna is able to bring out the ruling from the emotions of bina.**

In the *pilpul* of the *Gemara*, hidden in it is that this one says *chayav* and this one says *patur*; even an actual ruling there is theory, an abstract case, and you do not know how it applies to a particular situation. It is like *Gemara* versus *semicha*: even where the *Gemara* states a *halacha*, most people are very far from seeing the ruling. To see how the theory applies in a particular case is a thing of an *ish tevuna* (a man of *tevuna*).

phrases.he: ואיש תבונות היינו כח הקולט בכי טוב לעצם ההשגה,
phrases.en: A man of *tevunos* means the ability to really absorb the theory, to really internalize it, to really become one with the way you think and feel and view the world.

phrases.he: על כן מתפשטת ההשגה בו לעשות ולהורות בה כמה ענינים נבדלים לגמרי
phrases.en: Therefore, since this idea becomes one with him, it's able to spread out: he's able to use it, to make a judgment based on it, in many things that are totally separate from the theory.

phrases.he: וגם ביכולתו להביא את עומק בינה לידי גילוי כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: And he can also bring out the depth of *bina* and explain it in a way that's understandable, like we said before.

blocks.text: **A man of tevunos** has **the ability to really absorb the theory, to really internalize it**, so that it becomes one with the way he thinks and feels and views the world. **Therefore** it is **able to spread out**: he can **make a judgment based on it** **in many things that are totally separate from the theory**, **and he can also bring out the depth of bina and explain it in a way that's understandable.**

The depth of *bina* is just *tefisa* (grasping): you hold the concept, but it is separate from you, something you appreciate, not the way you think. *Tevuna* requires *kelita* (absorption): it sinks into your brain until you actually think that way. Then automatically you see it in all different cases ("How would I use this way of reasoning in this case, in this case?"), you can give examples and *meshalim* from day-to-day life to make the depth of *bina* understandable to a regular person, and you can apply it, because you really internalized it.

sections.title: Yisroel Saba and tevuna, Malchus of tevuna and the letters of thought
sections.summary: *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna* are the emotions of *chachma* and of *bina* as they come out into application: the intuitive feel, and the power to explain. *Malchus* of *tevuna* attaches the concept to words, the letters of thought, an outer vessel for analysis; and from it comes thought itself, *Leah*.

phrases.he: (והיינו בחינת אבא ואמא תתאין ישראל סבא ותבונה
phrases.en: And this is the idea that the lower father and mother are *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna*.

phrases.he: ישראל סבא מדות דחכמה ותבונה מדות דבינה
phrases.en: *Yisroel Saba* is the *middos*, the emotions, of *chachma*, and *tevuna* is the emotions of *bina*.
But these are the emotions of *chachma* and *bina* the way they come outside, to be revealed outside of the *etzem* idea.
And what's the idea of *Malchus* of *tevuna*?
This is the intellect that comes into thought.
This is called the letters of intellectual thought,
which the intellect is enclothed in this type of thought.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת כלי חיצוני למחשבה עיונית
phrases.en: This is the external vessel for analytical thought.

phrases.he: שהוא גלוי השגה דבינה עצמה מצד עצם השכל והסברא כו'
phrases.en: Which this intellectual thought is revealing the actual understanding of *bina* itself, relating to the intellect and the logic.

phrases.he: ומבחינת מלכות דתבונה נמשך שרש אותיות המחשבה עצמה שנקרא לאה כו'

phrases.en: And this is the large *dalet* of the word *Echad*.

blocks.text: **And this is the idea that the lower father and mother** **are Yisroel Saba and tevuna**: **Yisroel Saba is the middos, the emotions** of *chachma*, **and tevuna is the emotions of bina.** *Yisroel Saba* is application in an intuitive way.

blocks.title: Shatik Rav: the ruling he could not explain
blocks.text: Somebody has a gut feeling that this is the right thing to do, or the wrong thing, and cannot explain why. That is like *Yisroel Saba*. It is like *shatik Rav* (Rav was silent) in *Beitza*. The *machlokes*, he thinks, is on the difference between an egg laid on *Yom Tov*, which is *muktza* because it is *nolad* (newly come into being), and a cow born on *Yom Tov*, which is not. Rav ruled that there is a difference; they asked him why, and he could not answer. But he did not retract. He was quiet: he saw the difference intuitively. That is *Yisroel Saba*. Then somebody else came along and explained the difference: that is *tevuna*.

**But these are the emotions of chachma and bina the way they come outside, to be revealed outside of the etzem idea** (the idea itself): not the *middos* included in the theory, but the theory brought out into application.

**And what's the idea of Malchus of tevuna?** *Malchus* (kingship) of *tevuna* is the application into thought, speech and action. **This is the intellect that comes into thought.** **This is called the letters of intellectual thought, which the intellect is enclothed in this type of thought.** It is the external thing of *tevuna*: it attaches the theory to words, a language, so that you think about the idea in terms of this word.

blocks.title: The child's rubber stamps
blocks.text: Like a little kid with rubber stamps: one side has a picture of a cow, the other says the word cow. To write cow he stamps it, and it writes C-O-W. One side is the thing itself, the other the word. That is what *Malchus* of *tevuna* does: it connects the concept to the words.

**This is the external vessel for analytical thought.** Talking to yourself about an idea helps your mind work it over, but your mind works it over even without words. Talking to yourself is not the actual thought process of *bina* that makes you understand; it is a *kli* (vessel) to focus your mind on the right ideas. Your power of *bina* understands even without consciously thinking words.

blocks.title: Staring at the tiles
blocks.text: Stare at tiles in a very simple pattern, straight boxes or black and white checkers, and your mind makes all kinds of patterns out of them: diagonals, then straight lines, then boxes. The pattern is too simple, so your mind of *bina* keeps looking for more complicated ones, cutting it up this way and that way. That is your power of *bina* trying to analyze. Thinking it to yourself in words is like a *kli* to help your mind do that.

**Which this intellectual thought is revealing the actual understanding of bina itself, relating to the intellect and the logic.** In other words, *Malchus* of *tevuna* brings the actual understanding of *bina* out into thought. That is another thing *tevuna* does.

And from *Malchus* of *tevuna* comes the root of the letters of thought itself. Once ideas are associated with words, you can have the words without the thought: thought itself, called *Leah*, explained later. **And this is the large dalet of the word Echad**: *Leah*, as it comes from *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

sections.title: Ben u'vas: tevuna's three dimensions, and the lower mother who gives birth to the emotions
sections.summary: *Tevuna* has its own depth, length and width: its depth is *kelita*, absorbing the idea; its length is bringing it down into something else, a ruling, an invention, a skill; its width is thinking it in many ways. Its letters spell *ben u'vas*, son and daughter, because the emotions are actually born from *tevuna*, the lower mother, and not from *bina*, the upper mother.

phrases.en: And this is what is called *tevuna*,
which *tevuna* has the letters of *ben u'vas*,

phrases.he: להיות כי גם בתבונה יש ג' דברים,
phrases.en: because *tevuna* also has three things:
a depth, a length, and a width.

blocks.text: **And this is what is called tevuna, which tevuna has the letters of ben u'vas** (son and daughter): *beis*, *tav* and *nun*, with the *vav*, and an extra *hei*. **Because tevuna also has three things: a depth, a length, and a width**, like the dimensions of *chachma*, *bina* and *daas* in the first chapter. *Ben u'vas* means that *tevuna* is a source of the *middos*, explained shortly.

phrases.he: העומק הוא עצם כח התבונה הזאת שבאותה ההשגה,
phrases.en: The depth of *tevuna* is the essence of the power of *tevuna* in this understanding,

phrases.he: כמו שהיא בשעה שקולטת אותה כו'
phrases.en: the way that it is at the time that you absorb it.

phrases.he: ובה יוכל עומק ההשגה הנזכר לעיל לבוא לגלוי,
phrases.en: And when a person has this, that they really absorb the idea, then they're able to bring the depth out to reveal it,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בפסוק איש תבונה ידלנה כו'
phrases.en: like we explained before about how a man of *tevuna* can draw out the deep waters.

blocks.text: **The depth of tevuna is the essence of the power of tevuna in this understanding**: the type of understanding that lets you apply what you understand, **the way that it is** at **the time that you absorb it**. The main thing of *tevuna* is the *kelita* (absorption). *Hasaga* (comprehension) grasps the idea and holds it, outside of you; *tevuna* requires that you are *koleit* the idea, that you absorb it.

blocks.title: The Rav who goes over the Shulchan Aruch
blocks.text: It is not something you grasp outside of you; it has to be the way you think and see things. A *Rav* who wants to *paskin* (rule on) *halacha* cannot just learn a *halacha* and understand it. He has to go over, say, the Alter Rebbe's *Shulchan Aruch* over and over, until he thinks in its logic, its order and its categories. When he sees things through the eyes of the *halacha*, he can *paskin* in different situations, because he sees beyond the textbook. The same with anything: when you really absorb it, you can apply it.

**And when a person has this, that they really absorb the idea, then they're able to bring the depth out to reveal it**, to explain it so that it seems simple, **like we explained before about how a man of tevuna** *davka* **can draw out the deep waters**. So the depth of *tevuna* is this *kelita*, really internalizing the idea into your way of thinking.

phrases.en: the length of *tevuna*
is to bring the idea down into something else, a different subject, a different idea,
which is separate from the original idea that you're studying,

phrases.he: להורות בו ולעשות מעשים רבים על ידה כו'
phrases.en: to give advice based on it, or to *paskin* based on it, and to do many different things with it.

blocks.text: **The length of tevuna is to bring the idea down into something else**, a different subject **separate from the original idea that you're studying**, **to give advice based on it, or to paskin based on it, and to do many different things with it**: to apply it in your life, or to take some theory and find a way to make money out of it.

blocks.title: The Greek steam engine and the American steamboat
blocks.text: The ancient Greeks invented a type of steam engine, but it was not applied until much later, in America, as a steamboat. There were technical limitations, but it was also a mindset: the Greeks learned in the way of pure science, just to understand things; in America, at a certain time, there was a very big push to invent things and develop technology. That is more *tevuna* thinking.

blocks.title: From relativity to the bomb
blocks.text: The same with how they went from the theory of relativity to the atomic bomb. Einstein's theory was very nice, but just a theory; some physicists were happy it explains things. Then he realized that based on it you could make a bomb. They called the president: "you better make this bomb before the Russians make it." So they started the Manhattan Project. That is the length of *tevuna*: once you absorb an idea, you can apply it.

sensitivity.reason: A historical slip printed under his name: the warning to the president was about Germany, not the Russians.
sensitivity.publishable: The same with how they went from the theory of relativity to the atomic bomb. Einstein's theory was very nice, but just a theory; some physicists were happy it explains things. Then he realized that based on it you could make a bomb. They called the president: "We could make a bomb, and you should make this bomb." So they started the Manhattan Project. That is the length of *tevuna*: once you absorb an idea, you can apply it.

blocks.text: In a way this is the most important thing for anybody learning a skill, a doctor, a lawyer, a mechanic: he has to really absorb the lessons, and then he can use his understanding to do things or to give somebody advice. The same with a *Rav*, and the same with *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching): to apply it, the main thing is *tevuna*. But that is explained in the next chapter.

phrases.en: And the width:

phrases.he: הוא בחינת התפשטות התבונה בעצם ההשגה,
phrases.en: the width of *tevuna* is to expand, to spread out the idea within the idea itself, to apply the theory within the understanding,

phrases.he: להרחיבה במחשבה בכמה רבוי אופנים שונים
phrases.en: that you should be able to think about the idea in many different ways,
and not just the way it is alone.

blocks.text: **And the width: the width of tevuna is to expand, to spread out the idea within the idea itself**, **that you should be able to think about the idea in many different ways, and not just the way it is alone.** With *tevuna* you are not bound to the terms in which you first learned the concept: you find all different examples, explanations, stories and ways to think about it, and to explain it.

phrases.en: And this, that *tevuna* includes within it *ben* and *bas*,

phrases.he: היינו מה שמתבונה דוקא יולדו המדות בגלוי מהות בפני עצמם,
phrases.en: this represents that specifically from *tevuna* the *middos* are revealed, that they come out to be their own: the source of having an actual emotion, of actual love and actual fear, separate from your intellect, is from *tevuna*.

phrases.he: כי מבינה עצמה לא היו תולדות המדות
phrases.en: Because from *bina* itself the emotions would not be born, they would not come out,

phrases.he: אף על פי שנקרא אם הבנים כו'
phrases.en: even though *bina* is called the mother of the children, which means that it is the source of the emotions,
but it's the upper mother.

blocks.text: **And this, that tevuna includes within it ben and bas, this represents that specifically from tevuna the middos are revealed, that they come out to be their own**: actual love and actual fear, separate from your intellect. Not that the mind stops ruling, it is always *moach shalit al halev* (the mind rules the heart), but that you actually feel an emotion, unlike the *middos* of *bina* earlier in this chapter, which stay within the theory of the *sevara*.

blocks.title: Whoever takes from his fellow
blocks.text: In theory a *sevara* in the *Gemara* says this man is responsible, but you do not know how to apply it to this case. You know a rule, *hamotzi mechaveiro alav hara'aya* (whoever takes from his fellow must bring the proof), but here you are not sure who is taking from whom, so you cannot *paskin*. The emotion is hidden within the theory; when you know how to apply it, the emotion can come out of the understanding.

So *davka* from *tevuna* the *middos* come out, **because from bina itself the emotions would not be born**, **even though bina is called the mother of the children**, their source, **but it's the upper mother**, *Ima ila'a*: not the direct source. For something to affect you, you have to understand how it applies to you. You have to have the *uvchein* ("and so": the conclusion).

phrases.he: מה שאין כן התבונה נקרא אימא תתאה
phrases.en: But *tevuna* is called the lower mother,
to give birth to the *middos*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת ב''ן וב''ת, אהבה ויראה,
phrases.en: And this is the idea of *ben u'vas*, love and fear,
that they are included in *tevuna* specifically,

phrases.he: שהיא בחינת התפשטות אור הבינה למטה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: which *tevuna* is the spreading of the light of *bina* below, to everything separate from *bina*.

blocks.text: **But tevuna is called the lower mother**, *Ima tata'a*, which is like the thing of the *uvchein*, **to give birth to the middos.**

blocks.title: The upper mother and the womb
blocks.text: It is like a person: there is really one mother, and *bina* and *tevuna* are two parts of the same thing. When you speak of somebody's mother you mainly mean her intellect, emotions and personality, her head and heart: that is the upper mother. But the actual birth of a child comes from the womb, the lower mother. So *bina* is called the mother of the children, because it is their real source, but the actual birth of the children comes only from *tevuna*. We do not focus on *tevuna* as its own thing, because doing *hisbonenus* will bring you to *tevuna*, which has not been discussed yet.

**And this is the idea of ben u'vas, love and fear, that they are included in tevuna** *davka*, **which tevuna is the spreading of the light of bina below, to everything separate from bina.** *Tevuna* applies the *sechel* to tell you whether a situation calls for *chesed* or *gevura*.

blocks.title: The lion in the classroom
blocks.text: A kid in school learns about Shimshon and the lion: the teacher tells him lions have big teeth, how strong they are, what a miracle it was that Shimshon killed one. Now he understands what a lion is. If he thinks about it, he has *tevuna*: "Whoa, lions are dangerous. Therefore, the *uvchein*: I should be scared of the lion." But he feels no fear, because there is no lion in the room. He has no *daas* for it; it does not relate to him. When the lion walks into the room, his *daas* connects his *tevuna* to the actual emotion.

But even before he has a *daas*, the real emotion is the *tevuna*: your mind saying this thing is dangerous, if it comes near you, get away. There the *moach* (mind) tells the *lev* (heart) what to do: *moach shalit al halev*. The heart gets excited only when it is relevant right now, but that is where the *midda* comes from.

sections.title: The intellect of the emotions comes from tevuna, which keeps them going
sections.summary: The *mochin* of the *middos*, the intellect that tells an emotion how to go and keeps it going, come from *tevuna*: G-d maintains the heavens, fire and water, with *tevuna*. *Tevuna* is the intermediary that turns the *middos* of *bina*, which have nothing to do with a particular case, into what I should feel now.

phrases.he: וגם לזה הטעם בחינת המוחין שבמדות נמשך מבחינת התבונה
phrases.en: And this is also the reason why the intellect of the emotions comes from *tevuna*,
as it says, G-d founded the earth with *chachma*,
because the father founds the daughter.

blocks.text: **And this is also the reason why the intellect of the emotions comes from tevuna.** Once you have an emotion, its intellect tells it how to go and keeps it going. *Tevuna* takes the *sechel* down and tells your emotion in each situation whether this is good or bad: should you be happy or sad about this, like it or hate it? Applying your understanding of the thing and the situation to how you should feel is *tevuna*, the intellect of the emotions, and that keeps the emotion going.

blocks.title: The child who falls down
blocks.text: A little kid falls down. At first he is shocked, just thinking about what happened; then he calms down a little, it hits him, and he starts to cry. Why not right away? Because his *chachma* and *bina* were busy analyzing what happened, and while he was in the mind he felt no emotion. Once he calms down: "Wait a minute, that hurt me," and he cries.

blocks.title: "Hey, he hit me!"
blocks.text: If somebody is hit, sometimes at first he is too shocked to be angry: "What's going on?" Then he realizes: "Hey, he hit me! How could he hit me?" As soon as his *sechel* says, "Oh, you shouldn't let him do that," he starts to get angry. That is the way with every emotion.
**As it says, G-d founded the earth with chachma, because the father founds the daughter**: *chachma* is the source of *Malchus*, and the earth represents *Malchus*, as will be explained later.

phrases.en: He maintains the heavens with *tevuna*.

phrases.he: שמים הן בחינת המדות, אש מים כידוע
phrases.en: And the heavens represent the two emotions, *esh u'mayim*.

blocks.text: **He maintains the heavens with tevuna.** **And the heavens represent the two emotions, esh u'mayim**: *shamayim* (heavens) is a contraction of *esh u'mayim* (fire and water), *chesed* and *gevura*. *Tevuna* maintains them, because the *sechel* has to tell them what to feel, or the feelings go away.

phrases.en: And similarly it says, with *tevuna* they are established,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת קיום המדות בבחינת המוחין דתבונה שבהם,
phrases.en: which this is the maintenance of the emotions from the *mochin* of *tevuna*.
Because *tevuna* is like a sort of intermediary:

phrases.he: להביא מוחין מבחינת מדות דבינה במדות שבלב
phrases.en: it brings an intellect from the emotions of *bina* to the emotions of the heart.

phrases.he: שזהו כמו כח ההבאה בענין הנבדל, שהוא עיקר ענין התבונה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: That is like the power of bringing something out into something separate from the *sechel*, and this is the general thing of *tevuna*, like we've been explaining.

blocks.text: **And similarly it says, with tevuna they are established, which this is the maintenance of the emotions from the mochin of tevuna**: the intellect that tells the emotions what they should feel is what keeps the emotion going.

blocks.title: The tape recorder in the head
blocks.text: When a person has an emotion, a little tape recorder goes off in his head, repeating a certain thing over and over. Angry: "Oh, look what that guy did to me. I'm not going to let him get away with it." That is like an *uvchein*. A love: "Oh, I like this so much. This is so great. This is so great." That keeps the emotion going. People who want to hype themselves up do it for each other: "Oh, isn't this great? This is great." They want to keep the feeling going.

**Because tevuna is like a sort of intermediary**: **it brings an intellect from the emotions of bina to the emotions of the heart.** From the purely theoretical *middos* of *bina*, which have nothing to do with a particular case, to what I should feel now, you need *tevuna* to translate the *sechel* into an *uvchein*.

blocks.title: The chicken brought to the rabbi
blocks.text: The woman brings the chicken to the rabbi, and he says, "Well, according to the *Rema*, according to the *Shach*, according to the *Bach*," and starts a whole *pilpul*: it is based on a *Gemara*, this opinion, that opinion, it depends how you understand this and that. At the end she says, "So is it kosher or not?" You can understand the whole theory, but you have to take it to the deed: what does it mean in this case? That is *tevuna*.

Transferring something from intellect to emotions **is like the power of bringing something out into something separate from the sechel**, since the emotions are separate from the *sechel*, **and this is the general thing of tevuna**: applying the intellect to something separate from it, here to an emotion. So the *middos* of *bina* are in the theory, and *tevuna* applies it outside the theory. Next: how you get *tevuna*.

sections.title: The two nuns: hisbonenus, bina sheb'bina, brings bina out into tevuna
sections.summary: *Bina* has a bent *nun*, its width, and a straight *nun*, its length, and the name *nun* is spelled with both: the length is included in the width. The double *nun* of *hisbonenus* is *bina sheb'bina*, the intermediary between *bina* and *tevuna*: go over the idea again and again, in your own words, and you absorb it and get *tevuna*.

phrases.he: וידוע גם כן שיש נו''ן כפופה ונו''ן פשוטה בבינה,
phrases.en: It's known that there is both a bent *nun* and a straight *nun*, a long *nun*, in *bina*.

phrases.he: להיות נו''ן כפופה הוא הרוחב ונו''ן פשוטה הוא האורך
phrases.en: The bent *nun* represents the width of *bina*, and the long *nun* represents the length of *bina*.
And the letter *nun* is special: when you're spelling out the name of the letter *nun*, you spell it with a long *nun*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בשאר מילוי האותיות
phrases.en: This is not the case with any other letter in the Hebrew *alef-beis*.

blocks.text: **It's known that there is both a bent nun and a straight nun, a long nun, in bina.** The letter *nun* represents *bina*: **the bent nun represents the width of bina, and the long nun represents the length** of *bina*, because the bent *nun* goes out to a width and the long one just goes down.

**And the letter nun is special**: its *milui* (the spelling out of a letter's name) has a long *nun*: *nun*, *vav*, *nun*, a bent *nun* and a long one. **This is not the case with any other letter in the Hebrew alef-beis.** The only other doubled *milui* is *mem*, with a closed *mem*, whose significance comes later; *kaf*, *pei* and *tzadik* are not spelled with the long form. So what does this represent?

phrases.en: The length is included in the width.
The same thing with *tevuna*.

phrases.he: ואמנם נון הכפל בענין הנקרא התבוננות,
phrases.en: But the double *nun* that we find in the word *hisbonenus*,
like it says, "My people do not contemplate."
Which this *hisbonenus* is the inner thing of *bina*,
which is called analysis or study,
to dwell on a thing, on a matter, until you understand it clearly.

blocks.text: **The length is included in the width.** The *milui* of a letter is its explanation. Point to a bent *nun* on a page and ask what letter it is, and you say "*nun*": *nun*, *vav*, *nun*, a bent *nun* and a straight one. The explanation of a bent *nun* includes a long *nun*. So when you study an idea's width, with many different explanations, you start to get the length: you can explain it simply too.

**The same thing with tevuna.** Its length, applying the idea outside itself, doing things with it, giving advice or a ruling, bringing it to an emotion, depends on its width: explaining it to yourself in many ways, with examples from outside the idea. The width of *bina* is only the explanations and *meshalim* needed to understand the idea itself.

blocks.title: The motivational speaker's stories
blocks.text: Once you understand the idea, *tevuna* is like a good speaker who finds stories, examples and cute ways of saying it that are not needed to understand it. They help it sink in. Motivational speakers and inspirational books mainly give you stories to illustrate the point. You understand it already; the examples and sayings and "cute little quotes" help you feel it. Listen to any get-rich-quick tape: they tell you stories of people their program worked for, with all the details, and it gets you excited. "It's not really helping you to understand anything"; it helps you appreciate it.

**But the double nun that we find in the word hisbonenus, like it says, "My people do not contemplate."** Before, the two *nuns* meant doing it over and over until you understand it very clearly. Now we see they are a bent *nun* and a straight *nun*. **Which this hisbonenus is the inner thing of bina, which is called analysis or study, to dwell on a thing, on a matter, until you understand it clearly.**

phrases.en: This is called *bina sheb'bina*.
So this *hisbonenus* is the intermediary between *bina* and *tevuna*,
through the *nun pshuta*,

phrases.he: שמחמתו נקרא התבוננות כו' ודי למבין:

blocks.text: **This is called bina sheb'bina** (*bina* within *bina*). **So this hisbonenus is the intermediary between bina and tevuna, through the nun pshuta** (the straight *nun*). Of its two *nuns*, the first is understanding the idea and the second is bringing it out into *tevuna*. Doing the *hisbonenus* over and over, first you get the bent *nun*, *bina* itself; then the length of *bina* brings it out into *tevuna*: the straight *nun*.

So you get *tevuna* by doing a lot of *hisbonenus*. If you understand the idea in theory but cannot apply it, "you have to do the *nun* again": go over it a few more times. Study it more, explain it to yourself in different ways, and you will develop a *kelita* for it, absorb it, and have *tevuna*.

The bent and straight *nun* of *hisbonenus* are also two types of study. In *Kuntres Etz HaChaim* the Rebbe Rashab explains how to learn *nigleh* (the revealed Torah), *Gemara*, with the same system given here in chapters one and two for *hisbonenus*: two steps. First learn it until you can say over the words of the original very well. Then say it over in your own words. That is *tevuna*, the width of *tevuna* described before: saying it in different words, your own words.

Putting the idea into your own words, the width of *tevuna*, brings you its length; with the length and the width you get the depth, and that brings the *kelita*: you really absorb the idea. So there are two types of learning. In one you focus on the original, the *meshalim* in *Chassidus* or whatever idea, until you have it very well. Then, to get *tevuna*, you say it over in your own words and apply it to different situations and to your own life, and you start to absorb it: "a bent *nun* learning and a straight *nun* learning".

reviewQuestions.question: What makes the light of *bina* spread out into *tevuna*, and what does the shepherd at the well show about the man of *tevuna*?
Why can a *tafsan*, or someone who knows a *pilpul* with all its *sevaros*, still be unable to rule in a particular case?
If *bina* has *middos* of its own, the intellect leaning to merit or to guilt, why is *tevuna* still needed?
What are the depth, the length and the width of *tevuna*?
Why are the emotions born from *tevuna*, the lower mother, and not from *bina*, and what does the lion in the classroom show?
How do the two *nuns* of *hisbonenus* show the way to get *tevuna*?

notes.text: Phrases he reads without translating keep their Hebrew alone: the end of line 1 (v'nikra Ima tata'a), the second half of line 11 (he explains it in the next sentences), most of line 12, the middle of line 13, the end of line 17 (kayadua), the end of line 21 (v'dai l'mevin), the clause of line 22 on the root of the letters of thought called Leah (21 w1679-1729 explains it rather than translating it), and the end of line 37. Line 33's phrase cites his explanation right after the reading (23 w1014-1048), his only rendering of it.

The atomic bomb: he says the physicists told the president to make the bomb "before the Russians make it" (22 w844-876), and that "he" (apparently Einstein) realized a bomb could be made. Historically the 1939 letter warned of Germany. Kept as he said it. Flagged (other) for a public edition, whose text drops only the clause about the Russians.

Shatik Rav (21 w877-1045): he gives it from memory ("I think it's the machlokes"), as a dispute in Beitza over an egg laid on Yom Tov and a cow born on Yom Tov. A reviewer may want to check the source; the block keeps his account.

Shechita (20 w1317-1388): he says one may slaughter with anything sharp, even slowly all day, as long as there is no pressing or ripping. Kept as an illustration of the practical versus the essential; it is not flagged, but a public edition may want a reviewer to read it as halacha.

Sensitivity: two flags. The contrast between how yeshiva boys and girls learn kashrus (20 w1405-1568, women); and the atomic-bomb mashal's "before the Russians" (22 w777-914, other), a historical slip under his name. Left unflagged: the woman who brings her chicken to the rabbi (a stock scene; the joke is on the rabbi's pilpul), the Greeks' and America's mindsets, and motivational speakers and get-rich-quick tapes (said without contempt, as an example of tevuna's stories). The remark that it became popular to learn Gemara in the pilpul style is an opinion on a way of learning, not on people.
Kuntres Etz HaChaim (the Rebbe Rashab's tract on learning) is spelled here as a title; the table's Etz Chaim is the Arizal's book, a different work.
